title: Car Repair
victoryHeadline: Caught! Crystal's number finally added up.
acts: Vaughn's Auto & Alignment ran on strong coffee, a price list nobody had updated since the moustache trend peaked, and the general theory that somebody, eventually, would get round to fixing the actual cars. In the Garage, Anthony had commandeered the demo sedan for what he insisted was hazard-perception revision — his third attempt at the driving test loomed, and he was narrating imaginary cyclists into the rear-view mirror with the gravity of a nature documentary. Two feet away, Brock's boot had found the one patch of floor slicker than anywhere else in the building, and rather than step off it he had elected to stay exactly where he was, arms out for balance, insisting to nobody that everything was fine. Emilio, clipboard in hand, was on his third recount of the wiper-blade box, because every time Brock swayed and Anthony revved his mouth, the number in his head fell out and had to be found again.

Up front, Crystal had the calculator out and was doing sums on a two-berth caravan she had no immediate plans to buy and had already, privately, named — the kind of arithmetic you do instead of thinking about the actual day you're having. Vaughn stood by the desk in his usual leather jacket, mid-pitch about a loyalty scheme he'd apparently invented that morning, entirely undeterred by Crystal's total lack of interest. In the Waiting Area, Diane had abandoned the chairs an hour into what was billed as a ninety-minute service and was rereading the same paperback page for the fourth time, retaining none of it, when a short, heavy sound carried through from the front of the building. She looked up. Nobody else did — the Garage was too busy arguing about a shelf.

By the time the noise properly registered, the trio in the Garage had their own crisis to finish: Brock finally overbalanced and went down with a slap that startled Emilio into losing the count for a fourth time and startled Anthony into an actual, real, non-imaginary handbrake turn. It was almost a full minute before anyone thought to check the front of the building, at which point it became clear that whatever had happened there had happened decisively. Diane put her paperback down for good, the loyalty scheme died with its inventor, and Reception — moments before echoing with idle chatter — had gone very quiet indeed.

whereabouts.A: Anthony had climbed into the demo sedan to practise his hazard-perception commentary for a driving test he'd already failed twice, narrating hazards that weren't there in a voice several octaves too serious for a car park in a garage.
whereabouts.B: Brock had wandered two steps into the puddle chasing a dropped nut, and now stood perfectly still in a rapidly expanding lake of his own making, waiting for someone else to notice before he had to admit anything.
whereabouts.C: Crystal sat at the front desk with a calculator, pricing up a two-berth caravan she had no immediate plans to buy and had already, in her head, named.
whereabouts.D: Diane had given up on the waiting-room chairs an hour ago and was standing by the window rereading the same page of a paperback, unable to remember a single word of it.
whereabouts.E: Emilio was three boxes into a wiper-blade count that kept coming out different every time, and had started to suspect the shelf itself was against him.
whereabouts.V: Vaughn was up front by the reception table, mid-sentence about a loyalty scheme nobody had asked for, in the last ordinary conversation of his working life.

reveal: It was Crystal, in the Reception — and the trick was that she never had to stand up. The wheeled desk chair took one firm push off the counter, ran the length of the reception desk, and clipped the leg of the display table hard enough to bring the whole precarious tower down: a decade of laminated quote binders, a demonstration engine block, and the oversized trophy Vaughn had awarded himself for 'Customer Satisfaction' three years running. It landed on Vaughn exactly once, which turned out to be exactly enough. Crystal rolled gently back to where she'd started, calculator still in hand, sum still unfinished — she'd underpriced the caravan, having just worked out she could finally afford the good one, on account of what she strongly suspected, correctly, the will was about to say.

escape.generic: The case went cold, the calculator eventually went back in its drawer, and the real killer kept sitting in that same chair every single day, perfectly still and perfectly reachable.

byAccused.A: Anthony was marched out still mid-sentence about brake reaction times, and never did retake that test — though for years afterward he maintained he'd have passed easily, if the day hadn't gone so spectacularly sideways.
byAccused.B: Brock's own verdict, delivered indignantly from the middle of the oil slick as they took him away, was 'I have been standing completely still for forty minutes, how is that a crime' — a reasonable question that nobody bothered to answer.
byAccused.D: Diane never did find out how that chapter ended: the paperback stayed on the waiting-room chair for a week before anyone worked out whose it was, by which time the real killer had already reorganised the whole front desk.
byAccused.E: Emilio was hauled off still holding the clipboard, three wiper blades short of a number that would now never be resolved, and to this day a supplier gets quietly blamed for a shortfall that never existed.
